name: Boolean
approach: TinyLanguage built-in primitive type 'bool' with literals true/false. No separate structure to build; demonstrate by declaring/using/printing bool values and logical operations.

name: Character
approach: TinyLanguage has no distinct char type; a single character is a length-1 string, obtained by indexing a string (immutable sequence). It is a representation primitive, demonstrated by indexing a string to read a char and foreach over a string's characters.

name: Floating-point
approach: TinyLanguage built-in primitive type 'float' (shortest round-trip rendering, whole-valued floats get trailing .0). No structure to build; demonstrate by declaring/using/printing float arithmetic.

name: Fixed-point
approach: No native fixed-point type. Faithfully approximated as a class holding an integer raw value with an implied scale factor (e.g. value*100); arithmetic done on the integer mantissa, rendering via integer div/mod to place the implied decimal point. Deterministic, no float rounding.

name: Integer
approach: TinyLanguage built-in primitive type 'integer' (decimal digits, no decimal point). No structure to build; demonstrate by declaring/using/printing integer arithmetic, div, mod.

name: Reference
approach: TinyLanguage class instances and arrays have reference semantics (Scope chain holds references; functions create fresh scope with no closure capture). Reference is a built-in representation primitive; demonstrate by aliasing two variables to the same class instance and mutating through one to observe the change via the other. No real pointers/addresses exist, but identity-by-reference does.

name: Symbol
approach: No native symbol/atom type. Faithfully approximated as a Symbol class with a global intern table (a dictionary class over parallel name/instance arrays): intern(name) returns the same identity-equal instance for equal names, so symbol equality is reference equality. Deterministic interning order.

name: Enumerated type
approach: No native 'enum' keyword. Faithfully approximated by a class exposing named static const integer fields (class const fields are static, reachable as ClassName.NAME), giving a fixed set of named distinct values plus a name-lookup method. Demonstrates ordinal values and round-tripping name<->value.

name: Complex
approach: No native complex-number type. Faithfully approximated as a Complex class with float Real/Imag fields and methods for add/subtract/multiply/divide/conjugate/magnitude; magnitude via the ** power operator (x ** 0.5) or a Babylonian/Newton arithmetic sqrt iteration (there is no sqrt built-in). Real working arithmetic with deterministic output.

name: Array
approach: Array is one of TinyLanguage's own built-in representation types: a dynamic array literal [a,b,c] with indexed read/write, foreach, len(), and growth via arr := arr + [x] or indexed-append at index==length. There is no separate structure to implement; demonstrate with a minimal declare/index/append/foreach/len/print usage test.

name: Record
approach: Implement as a class with named fields, a constructor, and a str()/print rendering of its fields; immutable-style record by assigning fields once in the constructor.

name: Product type
approach: A product type is the general 'combine N fields' concept that Record and Tuple instantiate; model it as a class holding the component values (e.g. a 2-field pair), constructed and projected by field. Re-lists the Record / tuple-pair concept.

name: String
approach: String is one of TinyLanguage's own built-in primitive types: immutable character sequence, index to read a char, foreach over characters, len(), and concatenation with + / &. No separate structure to build; demonstrate with a minimal declare/index/foreach/concat/len/print usage test.

name: Union
approach: A bare (untagged) C-style union overlays multiple fields on the same storage with no runtime tag and reinterpret-on-read semantics; TinyLanguage has no shared memory layout or reinterpret cast, so the faithful approximation is a single-slot class whose one stored value can hold any of the alternative types (object reference), exercising 'set as A, read as A' / 'set as B, read as B' over the same field. The reinterpret-the-other-member bit aliasing is the only part not reproduced.

name: Tagged union
approach: Implement as a class carrying an integer/string tag plus a payload field; constructors per variant set the tag, and a match/switch on the tag dispatches reads safely (sum type / discriminated union).

name: Container
approach: An abstract container (holds elements, supports add/iterate/count) is implemented as a class wrapping a growable array with Add/Count/Get and foreach iteration.

name: List
approach: Ordered sequence with indexed access and append; implemented as a class over a growable array (arr := arr + [x]).

name: Tuple
approach: Fixed heterogeneous group of fields modeled as a class with named immutable fields; covered by tuple_pair/tuple_triple.

name: Associative array
approach: Key->value map modeled as a class over parallel key/value arrays with linear or chained lookup (no native map literal exists).

name: Map
approach: Map is the same ADT as Associative array (key->value); re-listed under the same section.

name: Multimap
approach: Map allowing multiple values per key; class over parallel arrays where each key maps to an array of values.

name: Set
approach: Unordered unique-element collection; class over an array enforcing uniqueness on Add with Contains/Union/Intersect.

name: Multiset (bag)
approach: Set with element multiplicities; class over parallel element/count arrays with Add/Count/Remove.

name: Stack
approach: LIFO; class over a growable array with Push (append) and Pop (remove last). Tier B covers stack.

name: Queue
approach: FIFO; class over an array with head/tail indices for enqueue/dequeue. Tier B covers queue.

name: Priority queue
approach: Highest/lowest-priority dequeue; class backed by a binary heap in an array. Tier B covers priority queue.

name: Double-ended queue
approach: Deque supporting push/pop at both ends; class over an array (or doubly linked indices) with front/back operations. Tier B covers deque.

name: Graph
approach: Vertices + edges; class using adjacency list/matrix over arrays. Tier C covers many graph representations.

name: Tree
approach: Hierarchical nodes with children; node class with parent/child references and traversal. Tier C covers many tree types.

name: Heap
approach: Partially ordered tree (min/max at root); class implementing a binary heap in an array with sift-up/sift-down. Tier B covers min/max heap.

name: Array
approach: Arrays are a built-in primitive/representation type in TinyLanguage (fixed/dynamic indexable sequence). No separate structure to build; demonstrate with a minimal declare/index/foreach/print usage test.

name: Associative array
approach: Model as a class over two parallel arrays (keys + values) with put/get/contains via linear or binary search. This is TinyLanguage's standard dictionary idiom (no map literal exists).

name: Bit array
approach: No bitwise operators exist. Approximate by storing bits as a bool[] (or pack into int words and slice with integer div/mod by powers of two for set/get/clear/test); all bit manipulation simulated arithmetically.

name: Bit field
approach: No shift/mask operators. Pack/unpack named sub-fields of an integer via arithmetic: extract = (value / 2^offset) mod 2^width, set = arithmetic recompose. Simulates C-style bit fields without real bitwise ops.

name: Bitboard
approach: An 8x8 (64-cell) board normally held in a 64-bit integer with bit ops. Approximate the board as an int[64]/bool[64] (or int words sliced via div/mod by powers of two); set/clear/test and population-count simulated arithmetically, deterministic print of the board.

name: Bitmap
approach: A bitmap is a bit array (one bit per element). Re-lists the Bit array structure; implemented identically with a bool[]/packed-int backing and arithmetic bit slicing (no bitwise operators).

name: Circular buffer
approach: Class wrapping a fixed-size array with head/tail/count fields and modulo wraparound for enqueue/dequeue; full/empty detection. Standard ring-buffer build.

name: Control table
approach: Class holding parallel arrays of input keys and action codes; lookup the matching row then dispatch the action via match/switch. Data-driven control flow over arrays.

name: Image
approach: No graphics/file image I/O. Approximate as an in-memory raster: a class over a flat int[] of width*height pixel values with get/set(x,y) via row*width+col and deterministic ASCII/value print. No actual image format encoding.

name: Dope vector
approach: Class storing a base flat array plus per-dimension extents and strides; multi-dimensional indexing computed as dot(indices, strides). Faithful descriptor-based array access.

name: Dynamic array
approach: Growable array (vector): class with backing array + size/capacity, append via '+' concat or indexed-append at index==length, with doubling-growth bookkeeping. Directly matches the existing growable array-list demo.

name: Gap buffer
approach: Text-editor buffer: class over an array with gapStart/gapEnd indices; insert/delete near the cursor move the gap and shift elements. Deterministic content print.

name: Hashed array tree
approach: Class with a top-level directory array of fixed-size leaf arrays; index decomposes into (leaf = i/leafSize, slot = i mod leafSize). Append grows leaves then the directory. Pure arithmetic, no bitwise needed.

name: Lookup table
approach: Precomputed value array indexed directly by an integer key (or parallel key/value arrays for non-dense keys); O(1) retrieval. Build a table (e.g. squares/factorials) and query it.

name: Matrix
approach: 2D matrix as a class over a flat array with rows/cols and index = r*cols+c; implement add and multiply with deterministic print. (Iliffe/jagged form is the duplicate variant.)

name: Parallel array
approach: Several equal-length arrays indexed in lockstep so index i across arrays forms one logical record. This is the core idiom TinyLanguage uses for maps/records; demonstrate with e.g. names[]/ages[] kept in sync.

name: Sorted array
approach: Array kept in sorted order: insert via binary-search position then shift/concat; lookup via binary search. Faithful ordered-array build.

name: Sparse matrix
approach: Store only nonzeros: coordinate (COO) parallel arrays of row[]/col[]/value[] (or CSR with rowPtr), with get(r,c) scanning the entries. Deterministic; no dense storage. Distinct from the CSR graph demo.

name: Iliffe vector
approach: Multidimensional access via an array of references to row (sub-)arrays, i.e. a jagged array. Class holds an array whose elements are themselves arrays; index as rows[i][j]. No pointer arithmetic needed.

name: Variable-length array
approach: A runtime-sized array; in TinyLanguage arrays already grow via '+' concat and indexed-append, so this is functionally the dynamic array (re-listed Wikipedia entry). Demonstrate sizing an array at runtime from a computed length.

name: Doubly linked list
approach: Class Node{value, prevIndex/nextIndex (or object refs)} with head/tail and bidirectional links; insert/remove/traverse-forward-and-back. Single inheritance + this + null refs are sufficient.

name: Array list
approach: Growable dynamic array backed by the built-in array; append via arr := arr + [x] / indexed-append at index==length; tracks logical count vs capacity.

name: Linked list
approach: Singly linked chain: Node{value, next} class with head pointer; insert/delete/search/length traversal.

name: Association list
approach: Key/value pairs modeled as a class over parallel arrays (no map literal needed); linear lookup, add, update, remove.

name: Self-organizing list
approach: List class that reorders on access (move-to-front / transpose heuristic) to speed repeated lookups; deterministic given a fixed access sequence.

name: Skip list
approach: Probabilistic multi-level linked structure; randomized node level is generated by an in-program seeded LCG (never system RNG) to keep output deterministic. Levels/links and search-with-express-lanes are otherwise faithful.

name: Unrolled linked list
approach: Linked nodes each holding a small bounded array of elements; insert splits a full node, traversal walks nodes then their inner arrays.

name: VList
approach: Persistent list as a chain of geometrically growing array blocks; O(1) head-cons and indexed access by walking block sizes. Modeled as a class of blocks.

name: Conc-tree list
approach: Balanced tree of concatenable chunks (leaf/conc nodes) supporting O(log n) concat and indexed access; node classes with level/size and rebalancing on append.

name: Xor linked list
approach: Classic form stores prev XOR next in one field, but TinyLanguage has NO bitwise operators at all. Faithful approximation per existing corpus: keep explicit prev/next index arrays (or two link fields) to recover both neighbors; bidirectional traversal semantics preserved without real XOR.

name: Zipper
approach: Functional list cursor: a focus element plus reversed-left context and right context lists; move-left/right/insert/delete rebuild the focus in O(1). Class holding three fields; no closures needed.

name: Doubly connected edge list
approach: Half-edge mesh representation: Vertex/HalfEdge/Face classes linked by twin/next/prev/origin/incidentFace index references; supports face/edge traversal of a planar subdivision.

name: Difference list
approach: The canonical implementation is a closure (a function awaiting its tail) for O(1) append; TinyLanguage has NO closures (lambda sees only globals + own params). Approximated by a class that holds the accumulated prefix and an explicit tail placeholder, performing constant-time append and a final materialize step — same O(1)-append semantics without the function-as-data representation.

name: Free list
approach: Allocator over a fixed slab array with a free-index stack/linked free chain; allocate pops a free slot, free pushes it back, reuse demonstrated deterministically.

name: AA tree
approach: Self-balancing BST with level field; skew/split rebalancing via class with left/right/level fields. Directly implementable.

name: AVL tree
approach: Height-balanced BST with single/double rotations; node class with left/right/height, recursive insert/delete. Tier B covers AVL/red-black.

name: Binary search tree
approach: Node class with left/right and value; recursive insert/search/delete/in-order traversal. Iterative variant exists too.

name: Binary tree
approach: Node class with left/right child references; build a tree and run pre/in/post-order traversals.

name: Cartesian tree
approach: Tree built from a sequence honoring heap order on a secondary key; node class with value/priority/left/right, recursive build.

name: Conc-tree list
approach: Re-listed under Binary Trees but already implemented as a list structure; balanced concatenation rope-like tree of leaves via node class. Reuses the lists-section demo; not a duplicate of another entry in this section (self-referential duplicate_of corrected to empty).

name: Left-child right-sibling binary tree
approach: General tree encoded as a binary tree via leftChild/rightSibling reference fields in a node class.

name: Order statistic tree
approach: BST augmented with subtree-size counts in each node enabling select(k)/rank(x); class with left/right/size, recursive maintenance.

name: Pagoda
approach: Priority-queue heap stored as a binary tree where each node points to leftmost and rightmost descendants; merge-based insert/deleteMin via node class with two pointers. Faithful pointer structure, fully implementable.

name: Randomized binary search tree
approach: BST with randomized insertion-at-root or treap-style priorities; use an in-program LCG for deterministic randomness, subtree-size for random selection.

name: Red–black tree
approach: BST with color field and recoloring/rotation on insert/delete; node class with left/right/color, recursive fixups. Tier B covers AVL or red-black.

name: Rope
approach: Binary tree of string leaves with subtree-length weights; concat/index/substring via node class. Strings immutable but rope leaves hold substrings.

name: Scapegoat tree
approach: BST that rebuilds the subtree of a scapegoat when alpha-weight balance is violated; node class with size, full-subtree flatten-and-rebuild.

name: Self-balancing binary search tree
approach: Abstract category; demonstrate via a concrete balancer (AA/AVL-style) maintaining height/balance under insertion. Re-lists balanced BSTs already in the section.

name: Splay tree
approach: BST with splay (zig/zig-zig/zig-zag rotations) moving accessed node to root; node class with left/right, recursive/iterative splay.

name: T-tree
approach: Balanced BST whose nodes each hold a bounded sorted ARRAY of values (in-memory DB index); node class with a value array + left/right + AVL-style balance.

name: Tango tree
approach: BST organized into preferred paths each stored as an auxiliary (red-black/splay) tree for O(log log n)-competitive access; modeled with node class + preferred-child marks and aux-tree cut/join. Complex but uses only references/recursion, no missing primitive.

name: Threaded binary tree
approach: Binary tree where null child links are repurposed as in-order successor/predecessor threads (with isThread bool flags); node class enabling stackless traversal.

name: Top tree
approach: Dynamic-tree structure over a forest exposing expose/link/cut/path-aggregate via a balanced binary tree of clusters; modeled with cluster node class holding boundary endpoints and aggregates. References + recursion only, no missing primitive.

name: Treap
approach: BST keyed on value + heap-ordered on a per-node priority; deterministic priorities from an in-program LCG, rotations to maintain heap order.

name: WAVL tree
approach: Weak AVL tree using integer rank differences (1/2) per node with rebalancing rotations/demotions; node class with rank field.

name: Weight-balanced tree
approach: BST balanced on subtree sizes/weights with rotation when a weight ratio is violated; node class with size field, recursive rebalance.

name: Zip tree
approach: Randomized BST balanced by geometric ranks via zip/unzip operations instead of rotations; deterministic rank from an in-program LCG (geometric rank via repeated arithmetic coin-flips, no bitwise needed), node class with rank field.

name: B-tree
approach: Standard multi-way balanced search tree: a Node class holding parallel keys[] and children[] arrays with split-on-overflow and merge/borrow on delete. Arrays grow via + concat / indexed-append. Deterministic insert/search/print.

name: B+ tree
approach: B-tree variant with all values in leaves and a linked leaf chain for range scans; internal nodes are routing keys only. Class over parallel arrays plus a next-leaf reference.

name: B*-tree
approach: B-tree variant with 2/3 minimum fill: redistribute keys to a sibling before splitting, and split two full nodes into three. Faithful as a Node class with the redistribute-before-split policy on top of the B-tree code.

name: Dancing tree
approach: A B-tree-family tree (ZFS-style) that DEFERS rebalancing until writes are flushed to disk. The in-memory search/insert/balance is faithful; the disk-flush trigger is approximated by an explicit flush() call (no real disk, single process, deterministic) that performs the deferred rebalance.

name: 2–3 tree
approach: B-tree of order 3: nodes hold 1 or 2 keys (2-node/3-node) with split-up-on-overflow. Faithful via a Node class with key/child slots.

name: 2–3–4 tree
approach: B-tree of order 4 (2/3/4-nodes) with top-down preemptive split; isomorphic to a red-black tree. Faithful via a Node class with key/child slots.

name: Queap
approach: Priority-queue structure (queue + heap hybrid) giving working-set-bounded extract-min. Implement as a class wrapping a FIFO list of recently-inserted items plus a binary-heap array for the rest, with insert/minimum/delete operations. Deterministic.

name: Fusion tree
approach: Core technique is word-level parallelism: sketch significant key bits into a machine word and compare via multiplication + bitwise masks/shifts for O(log n / log w). TinyLanguage has NO bitwise ops, so the sketch (extract chosen bit positions), parallel-compare, and most-significant-set-bit are simulated with integer div/mod by powers of two and arithmetic (per the corpus's bit-trick policy). Search semantics faithful; the word-parallel speedup is conceptual. Self-reference duplicate_of removed (a structure cannot be a duplicate of itself); it appears exactly once in this section.

name: Bx-tree
approach: B+-tree-based index for moving objects: each (location, time) is linearized to a single 1-D key via a space-filling curve, then stored in a B+ tree. The space-filling-curve interleave is done with arithmetic (like the existing Morton/Z-order demos), and the B+ tree itself is faithful. Time partitioning uses an in-program counter, not the clock, for deterministic output.

name: Heap
approach: The generic heap ADT (a complete binary heap in an array supporting insert/extract-min with sift-up/sift-down). Implement as a class wrapping a dynamic array.

name: Min-max heap
approach: Double-ended priority queue: array heap where even levels are min levels, odd are max; supports findMin/findMax/extractMin/extractMax. Implement as a class over a dynamic array with level-parity comparisons (level = integer log2 via repeated division, no bitwise needed).

name: Binary heap
approach: Classic array-backed binary min/max heap with sift-up/sift-down; parent/child indices via i/2 and 2*i (integer arithmetic, no bitwise). Class over a dynamic array.

name: B-heap
approach: A B-heap is a binary heap whose subtrees are laid out to fit memory pages for cache/VM locality. Page-aware physical memory layout is unobservable in a tree-walking BCL interpreter (no real addresses/pages), so we faithfully approximate the LOGICAL structure: a block-grouped index mapping (fixed-size 'page' blocks of the array, parent/child resolved through a block-offset arithmetic map) over a class-based array heap, preserving the same heap operations and deterministic output. The locality benefit is simulated, not real.

name: Weak heap
approach: Relaxed heap where each node dominates only its right subtree, tracked with a per-node 'reverse' flag (a bool array, NOT a bitwise reversal). Implement as a class with an array of values + a bool reverse-bit array; join/merge via the standard arithmetic Dancestor walk.

name: Binomial heap
approach: Forest of binomial trees with merge/insert/extractMin; nodes modeled as a class with child/sibling references. Directly maps to the existing demo.

name: Fibonacci heap
approach: Lazy forest of trees with circular doubly-linked root list, decreaseKey with cascading cuts, consolidate by degree; nodes as a class with parent/child/left/right refs + mark flag. Maps to the existing demo.

name: AF-heap
approach: The atomic-heap / AF-heap (Fredman-Willard) achieves o(log n) priority-queue ops on a unit-cost RAM by packing several small keys into a single machine word and using bit-parallel word operations (multiply/shift masking, most-significant-bit tricks). With NO bitwise operators and no real machine word, the word-parallel core cannot be reproduced literally; we faithfully approximate by simulating the small-key 'atomic-heap' bucket structure (a class over fixed-width integer-array words with arithmetic field packing/unpacking via mul/div/mod) and exposing the same insert/extractMin API and deterministic output. The asymptotic word-RAM speedup is not real, but the structure and results are correct.

name: Leonardo heap
approach: The heap of smoothsort: a sequence of balanced Leonardo trees whose sizes are Leonardo numbers, tracked by a list of tree orders. Implement as a class storing the array plus a list of present Leonardo-tree orders, with the standard sift/trinkle restore using precomputed Leonardo numbers (plain integer arithmetic).

name: 2–3 heap
approach: Takaoka's 2-3 heap: a forest of trees built from 2-3 trees of 'trunks', supporting insert/decreaseKey/extractMin. Implement as a class with node objects (child/sibling/parent refs) and degree-indexed root buckets, analogous to the binomial-heap demo.

name: Soft heap
approach: Chazelle's soft heap: a list of binomial-like 'soft queues' with controlled corruption (keys raised) bounded by error rate epsilon; deterministic given fixed epsilon and insertion order. Implement as a class with node objects, ckey corruption on fill, and the standard sift/meld/extract — output is deterministic with a fixed epsilon.

name: Pairing heap
approach: Multiway-tree heap with O(1) meld and amortized-efficient extractMin via the two-pass pairing merge; nodes as a class with child/sibling refs. Maps to the existing demo.

name: Leftist heap
approach: Mergeable binary heap maintaining the leftist (s-value/null-path-length) property; recursive merge of right spines then swap children. Nodes as a class with left/right/rank. Maps to the existing demo.

name: Treap
approach: Randomized BST keyed by key and heap-ordered by priority; priorities from an in-program LCG for deterministic output. Maps to the existing demo 00530.treap. NOTE: this is the same structure as the Binary-Trees-section Treap (a cross-section repeat), but it is the ONLY Treap entry within this Heaps audit list, so duplicate_of is empty (it cannot be a duplicate of itself).

name: Beap
approach: Bi-parental heap: elements in a triangular array where element i has up to two parents and two children; supports O(sqrt n) search/insert/delete. Implement as a class over a flat dynamic array with row/column index arithmetic (sqrt via integer Newton iteration, no bitwise).

name: Skew heap
approach: Self-adjusting mergeable heap: recursive merge that unconditionally swaps children on the way up (no balance metadata). Nodes as a class with left/right refs. Maps to the existing demo.

name: Ternary heap
approach: A d-ary heap with d=3: array heap with parent (i-1)/3 and children 3*i+1..3*i+3 via integer arithmetic. Implement as a class over a dynamic array (specialization of the d-ary heap).

name: D-ary heap
approach: Generalized array heap with configurable branching factor d; parent (i-1)/d, children d*i+1..d*i+d via integer arithmetic. Maps to the existing demo.

name: Brodal queue
approach: Brodal's worst-case-optimal meldable priority queue achieves O(1) worst-case insert/meld/decreaseKey and O(log n) deleteMin, but only via an intricate guide/redundant-counter bookkeeping scheme designed for the pointer-machine WORST-CASE bounds. The full guide machinery is implementable in principle but enormous; a single-file demo cannot reproduce the true worst-case bounds, so we faithfully approximate the meldable-priority-queue BEHAVIOR (same operations and results) using a simpler forest-of-trees core (binomial/pairing-style class with node refs) and document that the O(1) worst-case guarantee is not reproduced, only the API and deterministic output.

name: Radix tree
approach: Compressed prefix trie: a Node class holding an edge-label string, a child-array of edges, and an is-terminal flag; insert splits an edge on the longest common prefix, lookup walks edge labels. Pure string + class + array work, no bit ops.

name: Suffix tree
approach: Existing demo: a compressed trie of all suffixes built by naive O(n^2) insertion of each suffix into a radix/edge-labelled tree (Ukkonen not required); substring search walks edges. Strings indexable + class nodes suffice.

name: Suffix array
approach: Existing demo: build array of all suffix start indices, sort by comparing string suffixes (string indexing + comparison), then binary-search a pattern. Deterministic, no bit ops.

name: Compressed suffix array
approach: The real CSA stores the suffix array in succinct bit-packed form with the Psi function and rank/select on bitvectors. With no bitwise ops we build a plain suffix array plus an explicit Psi index array (Psi[i] = position whose suffix is the next-larger by dropping first char) and answer SA[i] by following Psi from the sampled head; the 'compression' (bit-packing) is simulated by ordinary integer arrays rather than packed words. Functionally faithful (same Psi-driven recovery), only the storage is not bit-level.

name: FM-index
approach: FM-index = Burrows-Wheeler transform + the C[] table + rank() on the BWT via wavelet-tree/bit-packed occurrence blocks. We faithfully compute the BWT from the suffix array, build C[] and an explicit per-character cumulative occurrence (rank) table as integer arrays, and run real backward-search count queries. Only the succinct bit-packed rank representation is approximated by plain prefix-count arrays (no bitwise/wavelet packing available).

name: Generalised suffix tree
approach: Suffix tree over a SET of strings: concatenate each input with a distinct terminator char and insert every suffix into one edge-labelled trie, tagging leaves with their source-string id. Same machinery as the single-string suffix tree, extended with an owner id per leaf; supports common-substring queries.

name: B-tree
approach: Existing demo: order-m node class with parallel key-array and child-array, search/insert with node split on overflow. No bit ops needed. (Re-listed here; the canonical B-tree entry lives in the B-trees section.)

name: Judy array
approach: Judy is a 256-ary radix tree whose node compression (Judy1/JudyL linear/bitmap/uncompressed node variants) is driven by population-count over 256-bit presence bitmaps. With no bitwise ops or popcount we model it as a 256-ary radix tree keyed by extracting each key byte via integer div/mod (byte = key / 256^k % 256), and represent each node's child presence with a sparse parallel (slot, child) array rather than a packed 256-bit bitmap. Faithful byte-radix lookup/insert; the bitmap-population compression is approximated by sparse arrays.

name: Trie
approach: Existing demo: prefix tree where each node has a child-array indexed by character (or a parallel char/child array) and an is-word flag; insert/search/prefix walk character by character. Pure strings + classes.

name: X-fast trie
approach: X-fast trie = a bit trie of fixed height w over universe [0,2^w) with one hash table of present prefixes per level, giving O(log w) predecessor via binary search on levels. With no bitwise ops we extract the i-th bit by arithmetic (bit = key / 2^(w-1-i) % 2) and replace each level's hash table with a class-based map over parallel arrays (the corpus's standard map model). Faithful level-search + descendant/predecessor pointers; only bit extraction and the per-level hashing are arithmetic/array approximations.

name: Y-fast trie
approach: Y-fast trie = an X-fast trie over O(n/log n) representative keys, each representative fronting a balanced BST bucket of ~log-sized clusters, giving O(log w) ops with O(n) space. We build the approximated X-fast trie (arithmetic bit extraction + class-map levels) over representatives and back each with a simple balanced-BST/array bucket. Same two-layer algorithm; the only approximations are the inherited arithmetic bit-slicing and array-based maps.

name: Merkle tree
approach: A binary hash tree where each leaf hashes a data block and each internal node hashes the concatenation of its children's hashes; verification recomputes a root and compares. The cryptographic hash (which uses bitwise rotations/XOR) is unavailable, so we substitute a deterministic non-cryptographic integer hash (polynomial rolling / LCG-style mix using +,*,% only). The tree structure, parent = hash(left+right) recurrence, root commitment, and audit-path verification are fully faithful; only the hash primitive is approximated. (The corpus's blockchain demo uses the same deterministic-hash device.)

name: Ternary search tree
approach: Already faithfully implementable: a 3-way (lo/eq/hi) character-split trie as a node class with left/middle/right child references; insert/search by comparing the current char.

name: Ternary tree
approach: A tree where each node has up to 3 children; model as a node class with a 3-element child array (or first/mid/last refs), demonstrate insert and traversal printing.

name: K-ary tree
approach: Node class holding a dynamic children array grown via arr := arr + [child]; demonstrate building a k-way tree and BFS/DFS traversal. Generalizes ternary tree.

name: And–or tree
approach: Node class with a type tag (AND/OR via a string or enum-like const) and a children array; evaluate boolean satisfaction recursively (AND = all children true, OR = any child true). Deterministic.

name: (a,b)-tree
approach: Generalized B-tree where every internal node has between a and b children; node class with keys[] and children[] arrays, split when full to maintain bounds. Same class-over-arrays approach as the existing B-tree demos.

name: Link/cut tree
approach: Full link/cut needs preferred-path splay forests; faithfully approximate with an explicit parent-pointer forest plus splay-tree machinery (existing splay demo) over index arrays, supporting link, cut, and findRoot. The amortized O(log n) preferred-path representation is simplified to direct parent walks; the operations and outputs are real and deterministic.

name: SPQR-tree
approach: Decomposition of a biconnected graph into S/P/Q/R triconnected components; build the tree as a node class tagging each node with its component type (Series/Parallel/Rigid/bond) and a children array over a small fixed input graph. The triconnectivity decomposition algorithm (Hopcroft-Tarjan) is approximated/precomputed for a small deterministic example rather than implemented in full generality.

name: Spaghetti stack
approach: A parent-pointer tree where multiple leaves share ancestors (cactus/saguaro stack); model nodes as a class with a parent reference, demonstrate pushing branched frames and walking each leaf back to the root. No closures needed.

name: Disjoint-set data structure
approach: Union-find with parent[] + rank[] arrays, path compression and union by rank, as a class. Already covered by the advanced DSU demo.

name: Union-find data structure
approach: Same structure as Disjoint-set (parent/rank arrays, find with path compression, union by rank). This is a re-listing of the disjoint-set entry.

name: Fusion tree
approach: A static B-tree variant achieving O(log_w n) by packing keys into a single machine word and using sketch/bitwise parallel-comparison tricks. TinyLanguage has NO bitwise ops, so the word-level sketching is approximated arithmetically (mod/integer-div extraction of significant bit positions, as the corpus does for HAMT/Morton); the B-tree shape and key lookup are faithful. Word-parallelism is simulated, not real.

name: Enfilade
approach: Xanadu's enfilade: a tree where each node carries cumulative offset/width info (wid/disp displacements) used to address spans in a document. Model as a node class with children array and per-edge displacement fields; demonstrate addressing a position by summing displacements down a path. Deterministic.

name: Exponential tree
approach: A search tree where the i-th level node holds up to 2^i children; node class with a keys[]+children[] arrays whose capacity grows per depth level, split on overflow. Class-over-arrays; deterministic insert/search.

name: Fenwick tree
approach: Binary indexed tree normally uses i & -i (lowbit) bitwise tricks for ascend/descend. With NO bitwise ops, the lowbit is computed arithmetically (e.g. i - (i mod next-power-of-two) via a small helper, or a precomputed lowbit table), exactly the arithmetic substitution the corpus uses for bit-trick structures. Prefix-sum update/query semantics are faithful and deterministic. No exact Tier C basename; Tier B: Fenwick tree (segment tree / Fenwick tree) covers the concept.

name: Van Emde Boas tree
approach: vEB recursively splits the universe by high/low bit halves (sqrt(u) clusters) to get O(log log u) operations. High/low splitting normally uses shifts/masks; with NO bitwise ops it is simulated with integer division and modulo by sqrt(u), a standard arithmetic substitution (corpus-style). Cluster/summary recursion, insert/member/successor are faithful and deterministic over a small fixed universe.

name: Rose tree
approach: A multi-way tree where each node holds a value and an arbitrary-length list of child subtrees; node class with value field + dynamic children array (arr := arr + [child]). Demonstrate build, depth, and pre-order flatten. The canonical variadic-branching tree.

name: Segment tree
approach: Class over a 2N-sized array (or recursive node tree): build, range-query (sum/min), point-update via index arithmetic. No bit tricks required. Tier B: segment tree / Fenwick tree concept is already covered, but no exact Tier C filename matches, so existing_demo left empty.

name: Interval tree
approach: Augmented BST class storing intervals keyed by low endpoint, each node carrying subtree max-high; overlap query by recursive descent. Directly maps to existing demo.

name: Range tree
approach: Multi-level BST class (primary sorted on x, each node holds a secondary structure sorted on y) supporting orthogonal range reporting. Maps to existing demo.

name: Bin
approach: Spatial bucketing: a class mapping cell coordinates to arrays of points via a flat bin array indexed by floor(coord/cellSize). Maps to existing bin/grid demo.

name: K-d tree
approach: Recursive binary partition class alternating splitting dimension by depth%k; insert and nearest-neighbour search with axis comparisons. Maps to existing 2-D demo.

name: Implicit k-d tree
approach: K-d tree whose node geometry is derived implicitly from an index into a backing grid array rather than stored pointers; class computes split planes from the index and grid extents arithmetically. Closely related to the k-d tree demo.

name: Min/max k-d tree
approach: K-d tree variant where each node also stores the min and max value of a priority field over its subtree, enabling range-of-priority pruning. Augment the k-d tree class with min/max fields.

name: Relaxed k-d tree
approach: K-d tree where the splitting dimension is stored per-node (chosen at insert, e.g. round-robin or by a seeded LCG) instead of fixed by depth; node carries an explicit splitDim field.

name: Adaptive k-d tree
approach: K-d tree that picks each split dimension/value adaptively from the point set in a node (e.g. widest spread, median); class computes spread per axis over the bucketed points before splitting.

name: Quadtree
approach: Recursive 4-way region subdivision class; node holds bounding box and four child quadrants, points inserted to the containing quadrant, subdividing on capacity. Maps to existing demo.

name: Octree
approach: 3-D analogue of the quadtree: recursive 8-way subdivision class over an axis-aligned cube, child index chosen by sign of each coordinate vs centre. Pure arithmetic, no bit tricks needed.

name: Linear octree
approach: Pointerless octree where nodes are keyed by a Morton/locational code; the code is built by arithmetic bit-interleave (multiply/mod by powers of two) since TinyLanguage has no bitwise ops, exactly as the existing Morton/Z-order demos approximate. Store codes in a sorted array.

name: Z-order
approach: Z-order (Morton) curve: the bit-interleave of coordinate bits is simulated with integer div/mod by powers of two instead of shifts/masks, matching the existing z_order/morton demos. This is the canonical Z-order/Morton entry (maps to 00620.z_order_curve), not a duplicate of any other entry in this section.

name: UB-tree
approach: B-tree (or B+-tree) keyed by Z-order (Morton) codes for multidimensional range queries; combine the existing B+-tree structure with arithmetic Morton-code keys (interleave via div/mod, no bitwise). Faithful approximation of the bit-interleave.

name: R-tree
approach: Balanced tree of minimum bounding rectangles; class with internal nodes holding child MBRs and a quadratic/linear split heuristic, leaves holding data rectangles; window query by MBR overlap. Maps to existing 2-D R-tree demo.

name: R+ tree
approach: R-tree variant with NON-overlapping internal MBRs (objects may be split/duplicated across nodes to avoid overlap); extend the R-tree class with clipping-on-insert. Same primitives as the R-tree demo.

name: R* tree
approach: R-tree variant with improved insert/split heuristics (forced reinsertion, overlap/area-minimising split choice); augment the R-tree class with the R*-style cost functions. All arithmetic on MBR coordinates.

name: Hilbert R-tree
approach: R-tree ordered by the Hilbert space-filling-curve value of each rectangle's centre; the Hilbert index is computed with the standard arithmetic rotate/quadrant algorithm (div/mod, no bitwise ops), consistent with the corpus's arithmetic curve approach. Combines R-tree demo with arithmetic Hilbert mapping.

name: X-tree
approach: R-tree variant introducing variable-size 'supernodes' to avoid high-dimensional overlap; extend the R-tree class with a supernode flag and overlap-threshold split rule. Same coordinate arithmetic as R-tree.

name: Metric tree
approach: Generic distance-based partitioning tree (parent of VP/M/BK trees): a class that recursively partitions points by distance to chosen pivots using a FIXED metric (Euclidean/integer) — TinyLanguage has no closures, so the metric is hard-coded in a method rather than passed as a captured function. Pivot pruning by triangle inequality. All arithmetic.

name: Cover tree
approach: Leveled metric tree where each level i covers points within 2^i of a parent (cover/separation/nesting invariants); class with per-level node lists, the 2^i radii produced by repeated multiplication (not bit shifts). Nearest-neighbour by level descent. All metric arithmetic.

name: M-tree
approach: Balanced metric tree (disk-oriented analogue of R-tree) whose nodes store routing objects with covering radii; range/kNN query prunes by triangle inequality. Class over a fixed metric, arithmetic only.

name: VP-tree
approach: Vantage-point tree: each node picks a pivot and partitions remaining points by median distance into inside/outside subtrees; range search prunes by the triangle inequality. Maps directly to existing demo.

name: BK-tree
approach: Burkhard-Keller tree keyed by a discrete metric (e.g. edit distance), children indexed by integer distance to the parent; query collects nodes within tolerance using the triangle inequality. Maps directly to existing demo.

name: Bounding interval hierarchy
approach: BVH variant storing only two split-plane values per inner node (one axis, left-max and right-min) instead of full child boxes; class recursively partitions primitive indices along an axis. Pure coordinate arithmetic.

name: Bounding volume hierarchy
approach: Tree of axis-aligned bounding boxes over primitives, built by recursive median/SAH split; class with node AABBs and overlap/ray-box query by coordinate comparison. Closely related to the R-tree demo.

name: BSP tree
approach: Binary space partitioning: each node stores a splitting plane (line in 2-D) and recursively partitions geometry into front/back half-spaces; class classifies points/segments by signed side via dot-product arithmetic.

name: Rapidly exploring random tree
approach: RRT path-planning tree: deterministic by sampling configuration space with an in-program seeded LCG (per corpus 'seed any randomness') instead of system RNG; class grows a tree of nodes, each new sample steered toward the nearest existing node. Tree + nearest-neighbour are exact; only the sampler is the seeded approximation.

name: Abstract syntax tree
approach: Class-based node hierarchy (NumberNode/BinaryNode/etc.) built via constructors with child references; a recursive Evaluate walk over the tree. TinyLanguage's own interpreter is built on exactly this pattern, so it is directly representable as a small arithmetic AST that prints both a pretty-printed form and the evaluated result deterministically.

name: Parse tree
approach: A concrete syntax tree: classes for grammar-rule nodes and terminal/leaf nodes, children held in arrays grown by '+' concat. Build a parse tree for a tiny grammar (e.g. arithmetic) and print an indented traversal. Distinct from AST in keeping all terminals/non-terminals.

name: Decision tree
approach: Class with internal nodes carrying a feature index + threshold and leaf nodes carrying a label; a recursive Classify(sample) walk choosing left/right by comparison. Deterministic; arrays of samples and a fixed/hand-built tree need no RNG. Corrected a self-referential duplicate_of ("Decision tree" pointing at itself) to empty; this is the canonical decision-tree entry, not a duplicate.

name: Alternating decision tree
approach: ADTree (boosting): alternating decision nodes (a condition) and prediction nodes (a numeric score). Model as classes; classification sums the prediction scores along every decision node whose condition matches the instance, then thresholds the total sign. Pure float arithmetic over a hand-built tree; fully deterministic.

name: Game tree
approach: Class-based tree of game states with a minimax (or full-expansion) walk choosing optimal moves; demonstrate with a tiny deterministic game (e.g. a small tic-tac-toe subtree or Nim). No randomness needed, so output is deterministic.

name: Expectiminimax tree
approach: Game tree augmented with chance nodes: max/min nodes recurse as usual, chance nodes return the probability-weighted (expected) value of children using float multiply/add. Probabilities are fixed constants in the program, so no system RNG is involved and output is deterministic.

name: Finger tree
approach: A nested 2-3 tree with cached digit buffers at each end, modeled as Empty/Single/Deep node classes (with measured monoid for size); supports amortized O(1) cons/snoc/head/last and concat. Implementable with class nodes + arrays; no closures or bitwise ops needed; deterministic. (Functional-persistence flavor; build it as immutable-by-convention nodes.)

name: Expression tree
approach: Binary tree of operator nodes and literal/variable leaf nodes with a recursive Evaluate; near-identical to AST but specialized to arithmetic/boolean expressions. Build (3 + 4) * 5 style trees and evaluate + pretty-print deterministically.

name: Log-structured merge-tree
approach: In-memory LSM: a small sorted memtable plus an array of immutable sorted 'levels'/runs; writes go to the memtable, flush to a new run when full, and a merge/compaction routine k-way-merges runs (dropping superseded keys). Reads scan newest-to-oldest. All in-process with arrays - no disk/concurrency required - and deterministic. (existing_demo is a loose 'closest related' map to the chained hash-table resize demo, which is in the demo list; the LSM itself is a fresh build.)

name: PQ tree
approach: Represents all permutations of leaves consistent with constraints via P-nodes (children in any order) and Q-nodes (children in fixed order or its reverse), with leaves; the Reduce(subset) operation restricts allowed orderings. Implementable as a class tree with a deterministic reduce/template-matching walk over a small leaf set; print the resulting frontier orderings.

name: Approximate Membership Query Filter
approach: AMQ is the umbrella concept (Bloom/cuckoo/quotient). Implement as a class wrapping a bit-array (modeled as an integer array of 0/1) plus k deterministic hash functions (multiply-add-mod LCG-style hashes); supports Add and probabilistic Contains with no false negatives. Set-bit/test-bit over an int-per-bit array needs NO bitwise ops. Deterministic output.

name: Bloom filter
approach: Class over an integer bit-array with k arithmetic hash functions; set bits on Add, test all-set on Contains. No bitwise ops needed (use index-per-bit array). Deterministic.

name: Cuckoo filter
approach: Faithful structure: two bucket arrays of small fingerprints, cuckoo eviction, lookup checks both candidate buckets, deterministic LCG for eviction choice. The DEFINING cuckoo-FILTER property is partial-key relocation: bucket2 = bucket1 XOR hash(fingerprint), an involution that lets you recompute either bucket from the other WITHOUT the key. That XOR is a bitwise operator (unavailable); approximate it by simulating XOR arithmetically (per-bit, as the corpus does for the XOR-linked-list) so the alternate-bucket involution still holds. Hence approx, not a clean yes.

name: Quotient filter
approach: Faithful structure (quotient/remainder split of a hash, slot array with is_occupied/is_continuation/is_shifted metadata, linear-probe runs). The quotient/remainder split is normally a bitwise shift; approximated with integer div/mod by a power of two (q = h / 2^r, remainder = h mod 2^r) since no bitwise ops exist. Metadata bits stored as separate int arrays.

name: Count–min sketch
approach: 2D integer count array (d rows x w columns) with d independent arithmetic hashes; Add increments one cell per row, Estimate returns the row-wise minimum. Directly maps to the existing demo.

name: Distributed hash table
approach: Distribution (multiple networked nodes, message passing) is NOT implementable (no threads/networking). Approximate the routing/data-structure essence single-process: a consistent-hashing ring class mapping keys to virtual nodes and resolving lookups, which is the testable algorithmic core of a DHT.

name: Double hashing
approach: Open-addressing hash table class where the probe sequence uses h(k) + i*g(k) mod m with two arithmetic hash functions; insert/find/delete with tombstones. Deterministic.

name: Dynamic perfect hash table
approach: Two-level (FKS) scheme as a class: top-level hash into buckets, each bucket gets a secondary table sized to its squared count with a deterministically-chosen collision-free hash (retry seeds via LCG until no collision). Worst-case O(1) lookup; rebuild on insert overflow.

name: Hash array mapped trie
approach: Faithful HAMT: 5-bit hash chunks index sparse child nodes. The 5-bit slicing and popcount population maps are normally bitwise; approximated with integer div/mod by 32 for chunk extraction and a child-presence integer array instead of a bitmap+popcount. Matches the existing HAMT demo's arithmetic-chunk approach.

name: Hash list
approach: Array/list of leaf-data hashes (the leaf layer of a Merkle/hash tree, optionally with a top hash). Class storing per-block hashes computed by a deterministic polynomial hash; verify a block by recomputing and comparing. No bitwise needed.

name: Hash table
approach: Core dictionary-as-class over parallel key/value arrays with separate-chaining buckets and resize on load factor; arithmetic hash mod capacity. Directly the existing chained-resize demo.

name: Hash tree
approach: Merkle tree: build a binary tree of hashes from leaf data using a deterministic combine hash(parent = H(left + right)); expose root hash and an audit/Merkle proof path. No bitwise required. (The blockchain demo uses hash chaining but this is a distinct full Merkle tree.)

name: Hash trie
approach: A trie keyed by successive chunks of a key's hash (the non-array-mapped predecessor of HAMT). Chunk extraction from the hash uses integer div/mod (no bitwise shift). Functionally equivalent build to the HAMT demo with full (dense) child arrays per level.

name: Koorde
approach: Koorde is a Chord/de-Bruijn DHT routing scheme; the distributed P2P overlay (networked nodes) is NOT implementable. Approximate single-process: model the de-Bruijn routing key-space and lookup hop sequence over an in-memory node ring to demonstrate the O(log n) routing algorithm deterministically.

name: Prefix hash tree
approach: PHT is a trie-over-a-DHT for range queries. The DHT distribution layer is NOT implementable; approximate single-process as a binary trie indexed by hash-prefix bits (prefix extraction via integer div/mod) layered over an in-memory key store, demonstrating prefix lookup and range traversal.

name: Rolling hash
approach: Rabin-Karp-style polynomial rolling hash class: maintain hash over a sliding window with add-leading / remove-trailing updates using a base and modulus (all integer multiply/mod arithmetic, no bitwise). Demonstrate substring search. Deterministic.

name: MinHash
approach: Class computing k min-hash signatures of a set using k deterministic affine hash functions (a*x+b mod p); estimate Jaccard similarity by fraction of matching signature components. All integer arithmetic; deterministic seeds via in-program LCG.

name: Ctrie
approach: Ctrie is a lock-free CONCURRENT hash-array-mapped trie; lock-freedom/CAS/I-nodes require threads/atomics which are NOT available. Approximate single-threaded: a HAMT-style trie supporting insert/lookup/remove (the snapshot/CAS concurrency machinery dropped). Chunk extraction via integer div/mod as in the HAMT demo.

name: Graph
approach: Generic graph as a class holding a vertex list plus an adjacency structure (parallel index arrays); add-vertex/add-edge/neighbors operations with deterministic iteration order.

name: Adjacency list
approach: Graph class storing, per vertex, an array of neighbor indices grown via arr := arr + [n]; the standard Tier B graph adjacency-list representation. existing_demo cleared: 00601 is the edge-LIST representation, a different structure; no dedicated adjacency-list Tier C demo. Tier B: graph adjacency list.

name: Adjacency matrix
approach: n x n matrix as an array of integer arrays; cell [i][j] holds edge weight/0; direct existing demo.

name: Graph-structured stack
approach: GLR-style shared stack: node class where each node carries an array of parent-link indices (multiple predecessors), enabling push that forks/merges; node pool in parallel arrays, deterministic traversal. No closures/threads/pointers needed - links are integer ids.

name: Scene graph
approach: Tree/DAG of transform nodes: a Node class with a children array and a local transform (e.g. 2D offset); traversal composes parent transforms additively and prints world positions deterministically.

name: Decision tree
approach: Tree of decision nodes (attribute test -> branch) with leaf class labels; classify by walking from root. Re-listed under Trees as well as Graphs - cross-section dedup is handled in the Trees section, so duplicate_of is empty within this Graphs array (a self-referential duplicate_of was incorrect).

name: Binary decision diagram
approach: Reduced ordered BDD via Shannon expansion: node table (var index, low-child index, high-child index) in parallel arrays, with reduction (merge isomorphic nodes, skip redundant tests) and apply; evaluate a boolean assignment by walking edges. No bitwise ops needed - children are integer node ids.

name: Zero-suppressed decision diagram
approach: ZDD as a BDD variant with the zero-suppression reduction rule (drop a node whose high-edge points to the 0 terminal) instead of the redundant-node rule; same node-table-in-parallel-arrays class, set-of-subsets membership test deterministic.

name: And-inverter graph
approach: DAG of two-input AND nodes plus complemented (inverter) edges; the inverter is a boolean complement FLAG on each edge (not a bitwise op), AND is logical-and of the two boolean inputs. Structural hashing merges duplicate AND nodes; evaluate by topological walk. Faithful, no bit tricks required.

name: Directed graph
approach: Direct existing demo: adjacency structure where edges are one-directional; supports out-neighbor queries and traversal.

name: Directed acyclic graph
approach: Directed graph plus a topological-sort method (Kahn's algorithm over an in-degree array) that confirms acyclicity; Tier B covers topological sort. Deterministic order by stable index iteration.

name: Propositional directed acyclic graph
approach: PDAG: a DAG over boolean-formula nodes typed AND/OR/NOT/LEAF (a generalization of BDD/NNF) with shared subexpressions; evaluate under a variable assignment by memoized topological walk. Node type held as an integer tag; logical (not bitwise) connectives.

name: Multigraph
approach: Direct existing demo: graph permitting parallel edges (and self-loops) between the same vertex pair; edges stored in an edge list so duplicates are retained with distinct ids.

name: Hypergraph
approach: Direct existing demo: each hyperedge is an array of incident vertex indices (size >= 2); incidence queries iterate the hyperedge list deterministically.

name: Lightmap
approach: Model as a class wrapping a 2D grid (array-of-arrays of float) of precomputed per-texel light intensities, with deterministic Bake (fill via a pure function of texel coordinates) and Sample(u,v) operations; print the grid. No graphics hardware or bitwise ops needed for the data structure itself.

name: Winged edge
approach: Boundary-representation mesh: a class over parallel index arrays where each edge records start/end vertices, left/right faces, and the four wing edges (CW/CCW predecessor and successor around each adjacent face). Same family as DCEL (00508); traverse a face boundary deterministically and print the edge ring. No bitwise needed.

name: Quad-edge
approach: Guibas-Stolfi edge algebra. The classic encoding packs the 2-bit rotation index into the low bits of an edge-record pointer and computes Rot/Sym via bitwise mask (e & 3 for the rotation, e & ~3 for the base). Bitwise is unavailable, so encode each directed/rotated edge as base*4 + r and implement Rot = (r+1)%4, Sym = (r+2)%4, with Onext stored explicitly per quad. Arithmetic mod-4 faithfully approximates the bit-packed tagged pointer (cf. 00657.tagged_pointer); operations and traversal output are exact.

name: Routing table
approach: As a pure data structure: a class holding destination-prefix entries (prefix value, prefix length, next-hop) over parallel arrays, with deterministic longest-prefix-match lookup done by arithmetic prefix comparison (integer division by 2^(32-len) is an exact logical right shift for non-negative addresses, so the masked compare is exact, not approximate). No actual networking required. Add/lookup/print routes deterministically.

name: Symbol table
approach: Classic scoped name->info map, modeled exactly as a dictionary-over-parallel-arrays class with an optional parent link for nested scopes (the interpreter's own Scope chain is one). Insert/Lookup/EnterScope/ExitScope are deterministic; print resolved bindings.

name: Piece table
approach: Text-buffer structure: a class with an immutable original string buffer plus an append-only add buffer, and an array of piece records (which buffer, offset, length). Insert/Delete split pieces and rebuild the piece sequence; Render concatenates pieces in order. TinyLanguage strings are immutable, which fits the original/add-buffer model exactly. All deterministic, no bitwise.

name: E-graph
approach: Equality-saturation structure: a class composing union-find over e-class ids (cf. 00644.disjoint_set_union_advanced) with a hashcons map (class over parallel arrays) of e-nodes (op + canonical child ids). Implement Add (hashcons), Merge (union + congruence-closure rebuild as a deterministic fixpoint loop); print canonical e-classes. No closures/bitwise/threads needed.
